The identical surface string placed in an isolated ordinary sentence stays near floor, as do tokens that finish or break the template and ordinary narrative words; partially structured sentences fire in the mid range.

Let Γ=(G,σ) be a connected signed graph, where G is the underlying simple graph and σ:E(G)→{1,−1} is the sign function on the edges of G. Let L(Γ)=D(G)−A(Γ), be the Laplacian of Γ and λ1\geqλ2\geq⋯\geqλn\geq0 be its eigenvalues. It is well-known that a signed graph Γ is balanced if and only if λn(Γ)=0. Here we show that, if Γ is unbalanced, then λn estimates how much Γ is far from being balanced. In particular, let ν(Γ) (resp. ϵ(Γ)) be the frustration number (resp. frustration index), that is the minimum number of vertices (resp. edges) to be deleted such that the signed graph is balanced. Then we prove that λn(Γ)\leq ν(Γ)\leq ϵ(Γ). Further we analyze the case when λn(Γ)=ν(Γ). In the latter setting, we identify the structure of the underlying graph G and we give an algebraic condition for L(Γ) which leads to the above equality.

# Closed form of integral involving Bessel $J_0$

I am trying to find a closed form (in terms of known functions) for this integral:

$$\int_{0}^\Lambda\!\!\! \text{d} k\, J_0( k x)\sin (k y)$$

where $x>0$, $\Lambda>0$, $y\in \mathbb{R}$

I was able to find a closed expression when $\Lambda\rightarrow\infty$:

$$\int_{0}^\infty\!\!\! \text{d} k\, J_0( k x)\sin (k y)=\frac{-\text{sgn}( y)}{\sqrt{y^2-x^2}}\Theta\big[y^2-x^2\big]$$

But I wasn't able to find a closed expression for the case of finite $\Lambda$. Do you know if it admits a closed form and if so what it would be or how to get it?

Thank you so much in advance.

• Getting rid of every useless parameter, you are just asking if $J_0(x)\sin(nx)$ has a nice primitive for every $n\in\mathbb{R}$. Do you think that a hypergeometric $\phantom{}_2 F_3$ function is "nice" ? – Jack D'Aurizio Sep 2 '15 at 16:57
• HI Jack, thanks for your answer. Yes, that's precisely what I'm asking. I would consider hypergeometric functions "nice" for the purposes of what I'm looking for, yes. I would appreciate any help you could provide on this regard. – Collector Sep 2 '15 at 20:08

readings.explanation: This pole fires retrospectively on a token that carries forward an extended run of templated or boilerplate discourse, such as a license and address block, a bibliography entry, exam or textbook scaffolding, a math derivation, a code idiom, or marketing spam, drawing on roughly the preceding thirty-plus tokens rather than the local bigram. The identical surface string placed in an isolated ordinary sentence stays near floor, as do tokens that finish or break the template and ordinary narrative words; partially structured sentences fire in the mid range.

This pole fires on any token continuing a conventional multi-word phrase or coordination regardless of surrounding discourse, so isolated sentences like salt-and-pepper errands or city-name mentions fire just as strongly as license blocks.

This pole fires only on a small set of memorized boilerplate bigrams such as Franklin Street or Software Foundation, so novel templated items like parallel-group in a methods section or a LaTeX command backslash stay at floor.

verdict.notes: positive_holdout: 4/10 passed; hard_negative: 17/20 passed; counterfactual: 6/6 passed; lookahead_consistency: 1/1 passed. Failed gates: sensitivity, beats_confound_baseline.
